item.title: Senior receiving tandem helps lead Saratoga Springs football back to Super Bowl
item.description: Saratoga Springs receiver Gavin LaFrance makes a catch during the Section 2 Class AA semifinals against Shaker last week. (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - Gavin LaFrance and Jaden Lockrow were both two-way standouts on the 2025 Saratoga Springs football team that advanced to the Class AA state championship game in Syracuse. This season, the seniors are playing even more pronounced roles for the Blue Streaks. Not only has their production level increased as starters at receiver and in the secondary, but they've also taken on stronger leadership roles. "Those guys put the work in during the offseason to get themselves better," Saratoga Springs coach Eric Hayden said. Saturday night at Colonie High School, second-seeded Saratoga Springs (9-1) looks to capture a second straight sectional title in a highly anticipated Super Bowl rematch against top-seeded Christian Brothers Academy (10-0). Game time is 7 p.m. "If we could pull it off, well, I wouldn't say it would be a dream come true, but I feel like it is something this program really needs," Lockrow said. "Back-to-back really would be awesome and it would show how far we came and how hard we worked. We need this." "We want to keep going and build for another week," LaFrance said. "It would be really special to win it again." The Blue Streaks denied CBA a fifth consecutive sectional title in 2025 with a 14-13 upset win. The teams met in Week 2 this season and the Brothers prevailed 21-14 at home. Last week, Lockrow produced three touchdowns in a 42-35 Class AA semifinal decision over Shaker. He scored on two receptions covering 66 and 13 yards, respectively, to go along with a 33-yard interception return for a score. The senior has tallied a team-best 15 touchdowns, including 10 on passes from senior quarterback Bobby Morris. Lockrow has hauled in 25 passes for 590 yards. He has also run the ball eight times for 92 yards and four touchdowns. The senior also tops the team with six interceptions at defensive back. "Honestly, I take a lot of pride in it, and I am grateful Bobby has that much trust in me to get me the ball because I am not as tall as Gavin," Lockrow said. "He still has faith and a belief in me. It makes me play better knowing my QB trusts me. I feed off that energy of belief." LaFrance, who stands 6-foot-3, tops the team with 39 receptions for 587 yards and six touchdowns. The senior, who also plays safety, has registered two interceptions. With the graduation of running back Ben Coryea, who led the Blue Streaks with 2,553 yards and 31 touchdowns on the ground in 2025, the offense this season had to lean on others. LaFrance and Lockrow have stepped up their play as perimeter threats. "They have meant a lot to our success this year," Morris said. item.title: Wales out to derail Norway's repair job in Oslo
item.description: Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy took over as head coach in July 2024 [Getty Images] As the first snow of the season falls in Oslo, the clean-up operation at Norway's home stadium is in full swing – tractors on the pitch, Norwegian Football Federation staff getting stuck in with their shovels. This has been a problematic pitch in the past, with even the great Erling Haaland questioning its condition back in March, before it was fixed during the summer. By their recent, historic high standards, Norway need something of a repair job themselves. Having gone through 2025 unbeaten and then soared to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, Norway have lost three games in a row for the first time in a decade. Granted, two of those were against Portugal, whereas their losing run in 2016 included defeats in Azerbaijan and Belarus. But this is Norway's golden generation. With Haaland, Martin Odegaard and a glut of other elite talents at their disposal, expectations are greater than ever. Thumping Italy twice on their way to World Cup qualification was one thing – their first major tournament since 1998 – but beating Brazil in their last-16 tie in New Jersey underlined their credentials as an emerging force in international football. So, when this Nations League campaign came around, Stale Solbakken's men were expected to be jostling with Portugal for top spot. Instead, they find themselves at the bottom of Group A4 with just one win from four games, level with third-placed Wales on three points but below them because of their head-to-head record. How do you stop Haaland? Wales show how it's done Odegaard backing Norway to avenge Wales defeat Wales' only victory of the campaign so far was against Norway in Cardiff a month ago, and on Saturday they are bidding to join Portugal and world champions Spain as the only teams to win competitive matches in Oslo over the past three years. "The way we look at it is this is the type of game we want to be playing in," Wales head coach Craig Bellamy tells BBC Sport Wales. "I see a collective team that you have to like but, individually, very much so as well. So that's a good challenge. "We've all been aware of their threat. The World Cup proved that. And I just don't see them going anywhere for the next five, 10 years either." There is much on the line for Wales and Norway in Oslo. While either team could still reach the Nations League quarter-finals, the priority is to avoid relegation from the top tier. Finishing third or higher would also guarantee top seeding for Euro 2028 qualifying, enabling them to avoid being drawn alongside the continent's heavyweights. "It'll go a long way to us having an opportunity of being seeded one, which is huge for us, but it isn't going to be given to us," Bellamy adds. "We have to go out there tomorrow and try and take it. item.title: Cavan Sullivan may not beat Lionel Messi to MLS MVP - but he's already among the league's best at just 17
item.description: Cavan Sullivan GFX - GOAL Nine goals, 14 assists and an MVP nomination at 17: The Union star is delivering on the hype, even if Lionel Messi remains the man to beat. In April 2025, Cavan Sullivan said the words that were so wrong - but still so right. "I wanna be a Ballon d’Or contender. I wanna win it. I want to be the best player in the world," before pausing, "If you think it’s too much of a pipe dream, I don’t really care.” The internet explodes. Reddit is on fire. Here was a 15-year-old kid who, at that point, had played less than a dozen professional soccer games, asserting that he could be the best in the world someday. Some called him arrogant. Others called him naive. But plenty more were simply impressed that an American could say those words with his chest, and avoid being laughed off the internet. That's the thing with Sullivan, as many a former pro has now detailed: he has the crucial combination of raw footballing ability and the right kind of cockiness. Sullivan is good - statistically the best MLS teenager ever - and he knows it. But there is no sense of a kid resting on his laurels here, either. This was always going to come to a head at some point, of course. Debate is one thing. And on Thursday, Sullivan became the youngest finalist in the history of the Landon Donovan MLS MVP award - and the first teenager to make the shortlist. One thing has to be established here. Sullivan will probably not win it. Lionel Messi is the best player in MLS, and the stats back it up. However, it is truly remarkable that a kid, now 17, can be considered among the best players in a league laden with vintage global stars and domestic products who have put in years of hard graft. This should be celebrated. It will continue to be. But it is also worth remembering that expectations simply have to be tempered if this kid - brilliant, brash and bold as he may be - is to reach his full potential. How good are the numbers? Sullivan's numbers for the Union make for fine reading. First, the football - because this is where it should all start. It is worth noting here that we are looking at under two-thirds of an MLS season. Sullivan started getting consistent first-team minutes in late May, right before the World Cup. He only became a true regular right after the World Cup. He has played 1,828 minutes out of a possible 3,060. He has started 21 out of a possible 34 games. As sample sizes go, this isn't the most significant. And the other MVP finalists - Messi, Hany Mukhtar, Guilherme and Evander - have all comfortably eclipsed that mark. item.title: Official: Spezia majority ownership stake bought by US billionaire Repole
item.description: Official: Spezia majority ownership stake bought by US billionaire Repole American billionaire Mike Repole has officially acquired a majority ownership stake in Serie C club Spezia Calcio, joining forces with Tom Roberts. This is only the latest foreign investment in Italian football, as several sides are now under the guidance of figures from America, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates. Spezia announced the takeover with a formal statement this evening , confirming that Repole has entered into an agreement to become the new controlling owner. Former patron Roberts will also remain as a minority shareholder. New Spezia era under American investor ITALY – JUNE 1: General view during the Serie B match between Spezia Calcio and US Cremonese Serie B Play-off Final at Stadio Alberto Picco on June 1, 2025 in Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) This club was founded in 1906 and went bankrupt several times, most recently in 2008, when forced to start again from the semi-pro Serie D level. Their last Serie A experience was in the 2022/23 campaign. They had been on the verge of promotion to the top flight in 2025, losing the promotion play-off final, but then crumbled last season and were relegated to Serie C. “Growing up in an Italian-American family in Queens, I was surrounded by the same pride, passion, loyalty and sense of community that I see in La Spezia,” said Repole in a statement. “Spezia is a Club with incredible history, tradition and passionate supporters, and that’s what makes this opportunity so special.” ITALY – JUNE 1: General view during the Serie B match between Spezia Calcio and US Cremonese Serie B Play-off Final at Stadio Alberto Picco on June 1, 2025 in Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) The current President Charlie Stillitano will remain in place and welcomed the advent of this new era. According to Forbes, 57-year-old Repole has a personal wealth of circa $2.5 billion, thanks to cofounding sports drink BodyArmor in 2011, as well as Glaceau.

item.title: Red Sox's Jake Bauers Deal Pretty Much Spells End For Jarren Duran, Masataka Yoshida
item.description: Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran The Boston Red Sox have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers. According to MassLive's Chris Cotillo , the Red Sox plan to use Bauers "primarily as their designated hitter while also cycling him in at first base in an effort to get Willson Contreras off his feet." If that's the case, Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida may need to pack their bags. Bauers plays first base and can fill in as a left fielder or right fielder. He'll be in the lineup every day, and if he's primarily taking the designated hitter spot, Duran and Yoshida will be bench bats or, at best, extra outfielders. The problem is, both will be very expensive bench players. Duran could end up getting $11.1 million in arbitration, per MLB Trade Rumors' estimate , and Yoshida is due $18.6 million next season. Those are some large figures for players who won't play regularly. The Red Sox have Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Bauers can fill in if needed, and if the Red Sox don't want him there, they may much rather give Kristian Campbell a spot as the team's fourth outfielder. Campbell is already signed to an extension and started playing well in Triple-A toward the end of the season. Regardless, Duran and Yoshida simply don't have a path to regular at-bats with Bauers now on the team. Not only that, but neither one is really irreplaceable. The Red Sox could move on from both and find a much more cost-effective bench bat or two on the open market. More MLB: Cubs Superstar Wins 2026 NL MVP After Historic Season

item.title: Tennessee on upset alert at Texas A&M, college football model warns
item.description: On paper, you wouldn’t think that Tennessee was in any real danger against Texas A&M. Not when considering the general direction these teams have taken this season. But one of the most cited college football prediction models is taking a different view. Model projects a very close game Oct 17, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Volunteers defensive back Dejuan Lane (10) celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the first half at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Looking over the matchup, ESPN’s College Football Power Index model still likes the Volunteers over the Aggies. But by a very narrow margin. After simulating the game 20,000 times, the model favors Tennessee to be just three points better than Texas A&M on the same field. That’s a much closer gap than most Vols fans would expect against an Aggie squad that has one win in SEC play. Normally, Tennessee is 13 points better than its opponents on average, ranking 17th in FBS in margin of victory. More: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 11’s biggest games Why such a close game? Tennessee has been extremely effective getting after opposing quarterbacks, but there’s one potential downside: the Volunteers have struggled at times to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket and extend plays. That’s where Marcel Reed becomes particularly dangerous. Tennessee’s defensive staff has acknowledged the challenge of defending mobile quarterbacks, emphasizing the importance of maintaining disciplined pass-rush lanes against Reed when he takes off. If Tennessee’s defensive ends get too aggressive pursuing the quarterback, Reed can step up, escape outside, and turn broken plays into significant gains. That creates two problems for the Volunteers: Scrambling yards: Reed can punish Tennessee when its pass rush loses lane discipline. Extended passing plays: When Reed escapes pressure, Tennessee’s secondary must cover receivers longer, increasing the possibility of explosive plays. More: SEC power rankings entering college football Week 11 The bottom line Texas A&M doesn’t necessarily need to beat Tennessee with traditional drop-back passing plays. The Aggies can use Reed’s mobility to neutralize some of Tennessee’s pass-rush advantage and force the Volunteers to defend the entire field. The potential breaking point: Tennessee’s inability to keep Marcel Reed contained inside the pocket. item.title: Man Utd handed fresh injury blow as Patrick Dorgu withdraws from Denmark squad
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-DEN-TRAINING - AFP Manchester United's preparations for the dawn of a new era have been disrupted by a fresh injury concern involving Patrick Dorgu. The versatile youngster has been forced to pull out of the Denmark squad and return to Carrington for urgent assessment. Setback for United's versatile star Manchester United are facing a nervous wait over the fitness of Dorgu after the 22-year-old withdrew from international duty. The promising left-sided player has been sent back to the club's training base following a failed fitness test with the Danish national team, cutting short his participation in the current Nations League window. Dorgu had only recently returned to action for the Red Devils, featuring in the dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last Sunday. That appearance followed a lengthy spell on the sidelines caused by a hamstring problem sustained during a clash with Wales back in September. Danish medical update on Dorgu Denmark's team doctor, Morten Boesen, confirmed the news on Friday, explaining that the player was not meeting the necessary physical benchmarks. Dorgu has made seven appearances for Manchester United across all competitions this season, scoring once and providing three assists. 'We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches,' the doctor revealed. 'He needs further recovery time after his injury, so we are sending him home for additional rehabilitation.' Pochettino takes the reins While United deal with Dorgu's fitness, Mauricio Pochettino was officially unveiled as the club's new head coach on Friday . The Argentine replaces Michael Carrick and will formally take charge of the team after completing his final duties with the United States national team, which include matches against Haiti on November 14 and 17. Pochettino's debut in the United dugout is scheduled for a high-stakes trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on November 22. The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss was visibly moved during his final US-based press conference, reflecting on the magnitude of the opportunity presented to him by the Premier League giants despite his recent commitments elsewhere. An emotional move for the Argentine 'It's difficult to talk now. I'm a very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision,' Pochettino told reporters as he prepared to leave his current post . Despite the difficult timing, the manager made it clear that the chance to lead a club of United's stature was one he simply could not ignore as he looks to fulfil his professional ambitions in England. The manager added: 'But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true. I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United. When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down.'

item.title: 3 predictions for Alabama vs. Vanderbilt in Week 11 road test
item.description: The first of three games remaining on Alabama 's regular season schedule comes this Saturday afternoon when the Crimson Tide travel to Nashville for a SEC matchup with the Vanderbilt Commodores. Despite being double-digit favorites, this is still a tough matchup for Alabama as Vanderbilt has played the Crimson Tide close each of the last two seasons. Vanderbilt even upset the Crimson Tide in shocking fashion just two years ago in Nashville, 40-35. This season's matchup though features two teams trending in different directions as Alabama comes to FirstBank Stadium sitting at 7-2 (5-2 SEC), while Vanderbilt is 4-5 (1-5). The Crimson Tide are also ranked No. 3 nationally in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, while the Commodores have dropped five of their last six games. Following are three predictions surrounding Alabama's trip to Nashville in Week 11. Alabama's defense forces multiple turnovers Vanderbilt true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis has thrown eight interceptions this season, and will be facing an Alabama defense that has excelled all year at creating turnovers, as well as currently leading the SEC with 13 picks. I'll predict the Alabama defense to force at-least two turnovers in this game, one of which is an interception. Tide running game has big performance Alabama's run game currently ranks among the bottom half of the SEC with an average of 143.8 rushing yards per game, but could be in store for a big performance Saturday against a Vanderbilt defense that is allowing the fourth-most yards per contest in the conference this season. With starting quarterback Keelon Russell currently dealing with an injury, I'll say offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb leans on the ground game Saturday, resulting in a big game from the likes of Daniel Hill and Trae'shawn Brown, among others. Austin Mack sees action at quarterback Speaking of the quarterback position, Russell is reportedly a game-time decision for Saturday's game, per On3's Pete Nakos and Chris Low , meaning that backup Austin Mack would get the start if he isn't available. I'll go with Mack to see action at quarterback Saturday whether Russell plays or not, as well as to impress in whatever action the senior does see. item.title: Real Madrid, Manchester United monitoring Serie A midfielder who could cost €25-30 million – report
item.description: Real Madrid, Manchester United monitoring Serie A midfielder who could cost €25-30 million – report According to reports from Calciomercato (h/t Bernabeu Digital ), Real Madrid are closely monitoring the situation of Scott McTominay at Napoli. The Scotland international could become available in the summer amid uncertainty over his contract situation, with Los Blancos among several clubs keeping an eye on developments. McTominay-Mourinho reunion? A product of the Manchester United academy, McTominay became a regular at Old Trafford precisely during Jose Mourinho’s managerial stint at the club. The 29-year-old midfielder developed a special bond with the now-Real Madrid manager, which might come into factor if the Merengues do decide to make a move for him in the summer. Real Madrid have been on the lookout for a new midfielder since last summer and links to McTominay have been doing the rounds for a while now. On Real Madrid’s radar. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) The Scotsman’s current contract with Napoli expires in the summer of 2028 and an agreement over an extension is proving to be difficult to reach. McTominay is seeking an annual salary of up to €8 million, a demand that has complicated discussions with Napoli. As such, there is a possibility that the Serie A outfit decide to part ways with him next summer rather than risk losing him for nothing in 2028. The report even states that the Partenopei prepared to consider offers of between €25 million and €30 million for the Scotland international. No shortage of competition for McTominay However, Real Madrid are not alone in monitoring the midfielder’s situation. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino speaks on USA exit with Manchester United move confirmed
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino speaks on USA exit with Manchester United move confirmed Mauricio Pochettino Begins Manchester United Era After Emotional USA Farewell Mauricio Pochettino has had bigger jobs, louder stages and tougher dressing rooms, but this one clearly hit differently. In his first appearance after being confirmed as Manchester United manager, he broke down while explaining why leaving the USA role was, in his own words, among the hardest calls of his career. United moved quickly after sacking Michael Carrick following an eight-match Premier League run without a win. Pochettino arrives on a two-and-a-half year contract and officially starts on November 19. That gives him one final assignment before stepping into Old Trafford, a USA fixture against Haiti, then straight into the deep end with his first United match away to Liverpool on November 22. Emotional Exit Before Manchester United Debut There was no corporate polish about Pochettino’s explanation. It was raw, awkward and honest. He said: “Normally it’s the opposite. You’re sacked and you cry because you want to stay. “For this case it’s the opposite. It’s a really tough decision, but at the same time I’m excited for that step.” That sums it up well enough. He wanted the Manchester United job, but he was not walking away from a failed project. He was leaving one he still believed in. Pochettino added: “The staff and the players, I want to say thank you so much for the last two years. “You made me feel really happy sharing an amazing project. It’s difficult now for me to finish. “We were very excited to share a project which we really believe in and are evolving together, it makes the decision harder. “It’s a sad decision but we are professionals, and we need to try to find the next step to make your dreams come true.” Photo IMAGO USA Record Shows Why United Moved Pochettino took over the USA in September 2024 on a deal that originally ran through the World Cup. After guiding them to the last 16, he earned an extension through to the end of the 2030 finals. Results were solid. Before the Haiti game, he had won 22 of 35 matches. That matters, because Manchester United were not appointing a sentimental figure. They were appointing a coach with a track record of building structure, intensity and belief. Pressure Starts Immediately at Old Trafford He also said: “We increased the federation and around the world too. “I didn’t prepare a speech; I am talking from the heart. We recovered our motivation and the capacity to dig deep. “I want to recognise the value from us and me. Big thank you. You respect your work. You never lie to us. That is a difficult decision but we need to move forward.” Now he does move forward. Manchester United have no grace period, no soft landing and no patience for drift. Liverpool away is a brutal first test, but at least everybody knows where they stand. Pochettino arrives emotional, ambitious and fully aware of the size of the mess. That is a start.

The Blaugrana side secured 300 million euros through a bond issue to finance the pending work on their stadium, one of the institution’s most important projects in recent years. In an official statement, the club said the operation closed after obtaining the necessary authorizations from the National Securities Market Commission (CNMV). Goldman Sachs acted as the sole placement agent for this financing. The 300 million euros will support the transformation of Spotify Camp Nou, the centerpiece of the Espai Barça project, with new infrastructure to offer fans a different experience. It will also offer expanded premium and hospitality spaces, aiming to diversify services and experiences for attendees. This new operation is part of the additional financing approved by the member delegates during the Ordinary General Assembly on Sept. 19, which authorized resources to complete the works and address the economic impact caused by the project’s delays. Although Barcelona has already been able to partially return to its stadium and play a variety of matches since last season, the remodeling still includes work to complete all its facilities and reach the capacity planned in the project. The project is scheduled for completion in late 2027 or early 2028, with a maximum capacity of 105,000 spectators fully available for the 2028-29 season. Completing Spotify Camp Nou is a priority for the institution, as the venue will not only be the home of the first team but also one of the club’s main economic drivers, thanks to its new seats, VIP spaces, and hospitality services. item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow during a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow could tie a significant NFL record on Sunday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Burrow has had four total touchdowns during Cincinanti’s four-game winning streak. He’s tied with Drew Brees (2018) and Dan Marino (1984) for second all time. Burrow will tie Peyton Manning (5) for the most consecutive 4+ total touchdown games in a single season if he accomplishes the feat on Sunday night against the Steelers. Manning set the record in 2004. While the Steelers had a bye in Week 9, the Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons, 34-17, on Sunday in Madrid. Cincinnati’s offense has been red-hot lately. Burrow, who has a 23-6 touchdown-interception ratio this season, has thrown three or more touchdowns in each of the last four games. Burrow also had a rushing touchdown against Atlanta, giving him four total TDs against the Falcons. To say the least, Burrow is playing the best football of his career right now. The Steelers ’ defense has turned heads this season as well, allowing only 16 points in their last two wins. “He works very hard at his craft, but he’s basically taken this entire team on his shoulders, and I think everybody down there would tell you that,” said Cris Collinsworth , who’s the color analyst for NBC’s Sunday Night Football and a former Bengals wide receiver. “From just analyzing football, it’s always been you got to have a little bit of everything, when Cincinnati’s been good in the past and my teams went on to the Super Bowl, it was Pete Johnson, Ickey Woods, James Brooks and we had that sort of balance.” The Bengals’ win over the Falcons moved them to 6-2 overall and in a first-place tie with the Steelers, who hold the tiebreaker thanks to their head-to-head win over the Bengals in Week 3. Most consecutive games with 4+ total touchdowns in a single season (2004) Peyton Manning – 5 (2026)* Joe Burrow – 4 (2018) Drew Brees – 4 (1984) Dan Marino – 4 pic.twitter.com/YiQUb7MWdt — ANA (@afcnorthaccess) November 12, 2026 The Steelers-Bengals game on Sunday Night Football in Week 10 will mark the first non-September primetime AFC North matchup between two teams with .750+ win percentages since 1975, according to Pro Grid Sports. The last time it happened was in 1975, between the Steelers and the Houston Oilers in the old AFC Central. The Steelers will be playing for first place for the second game in a row. Before their Week 9 bye, the 5-2 Steelers played the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8, with the Steelers’ 27-6 win putting them alone at the top of the division. The Steelers and Bengals have split their last two season series, with the Steelers earning the last sweep in the rivalry in 2023. The Steelers last won in Cincinnati in 2024. item.title: Giants’ Jameis Winston Sings ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’ in Failed Attempt to Trick Opponents Into Penalty
item.description: Jameis Winston Credit: Kathryn Riley/Getty NEED TO KNOW Jameis Winston tried to have some fun at the Commanders’ expense on Thursday night The Giants quarterback sang the chorus from the Baha Men’s “Who Let the Dogs Out” to try to draw the team offsides Despite his effort, Washington didn’t fall for the trick Jameis Winston unlocked a new level of quarterback behavior while trying to draw the Washington Commanders offsides on Thursday night. Inserted late into the game for starter J.J. McCarthy on a short 4th-and-1 opportunity, the New York Giants backup barked the chorus of the Baha Men’s “Who Let the Dogs Out” in an attempt to catch the Commanders by surprise. “Who let the dogs out?” Winston, 32, screamed at the line of scrimmage. “Who! Who!” The hilarious moment was not lost on the Thursday Night Football crew in the booth. “You got to be kidding me!” Al Michaels said as the microphones picked up what Winston was laying down. Jameis Winston Credit: Sarah Stier/Getty “What is he doing?” analyst Kirk Herbstreit joked. Alas, Winston’s rendition of the Baha Men’s 2000 classic did little to fool the Commanders’ defense. The Giants took a five-yard penalty and punted from their 11-yard-line — later losing the game 24-21 to the division rival. Winston’s antics hardly surprised his teammates or coach John Harbaugh. “Yeah, I knew that,” Harbaugh later said about Winston’s canine-influenced cadence. “That was part of the cadence there. That was part of the cadence. Teams do jump in those situations sometimes. That was the idea.” Following the game, the Broadway aficionado explained his unusual snap call. “Just practicing that with the team,” Winston told reporters. “The defenses are trying to jump the rhythm. Came up with that. Wish we could’ve got them to jump offsides.” For fans of the unconventional backup, the lyrical moment also came as little surprise. In a press conference last year in which he oozed excitement about starting as the team’s signal-caller against the Packers, Winston referenced Hamilton — and sang a line from “The Schuyler Sisters.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! “I want fans to know that I’m going to do my best,” Winston said earnestly. “Obviously, I’m going to have fun, but I’m going to execute — have a surgical execution — and just play ball, man.” He then broke into song: “This is something I’ve been doing since I’ve been four years old. Now, I get to do it in the greatest city in the world. I’m gonna be singing it with my son.” Read the original article on People
